source.title: Cessna Model 172N Pilot's Operating Handbook (1979 model)
source.copy_reviewed: Public scan cited in 04b_poh_reference/poh_1979_reference_data.json (teensinflight.org); the scan also contains an operator supplement for one UK-registered aircraft, which Phase 7 does not use.
source.method: Values below were read from the OCR text of that scan on 2026-11-06 and cross-checked against the page footer. Page numbers are POH page numbers (section-page).
source.second_copy: Entries marked "copy": "1978 handbook" were read on 2026-11-10 from the page images of a scan of the 1978 Model 172N handbook supplied by the author (no text layer: each value was read from the page itself). The two model years share these pages, except where a later check found a difference (the VFE rows on p.2-4: this scan prints 85 KIAS only, the 1979 scan also prints 110 KIAS at 10 degrees flaps; see docs/value-audit.md); where a later entry repeats an earlier one, the later one is the one that was read from the figure.

gravity feed; selector BOTH, RIGHT, LEFT, OFF; strainer; manual primer; carburetor
white 41-85, green 47-128, yellow 128-160, red line 160

rotary OFF, R, L, BOTH, START (spring loaded back to BOTH)

up-draft, float type, fixed jet, accelerator pump, idle cut-off, manual mixture
lean until RPM peaks and drops 25-50 RPM; above 75% power do not lean beyond peak RPM
mixture RICH, carb heat COLD, master ON, prime 2-6 strokes (none if warm), throttle open 1/8 in, ignition START, oil pressure CHECK
mixture full lean, throttle full open, crank; repeat start without priming
28-volt DC, 60-amp alternator, 24-volt battery on left forward side of the firewall
split rocker: BAT (right half) all power, ALT (left half) alternator
shows battery charge or discharge rate
red LOW VOLTAGE light below ammeter; ACU removes alternator field on over-voltage; reset by recycling master; may illuminate at low RPM with load
avionics OFF, master OFF (both), master ON, light CHECK OFF, avionics ON; if again: alternator OFF, non-essential equipment OFF, terminate flight
airspeed 65 KIAS, carb heat ON, fuel selector BOTH, mixture RICH, ignition BOTH (or START if prop stopped), primer IN and LOCKED
alternate static source valve PULL ON; consult calibration tables in Section 5
flaps up, heater/vents and windows closed: 40->39, 50->51, ... 100->101, 140->141 KIAS
pitot tube on lower surface of left wing; static port lower left side of forward fuselage; optional heated pitot; optional alternate static valve below the throttle
gradual RPM loss; full throttle and full carb heat until smooth, then remove heat
engine-driven vacuum pump powers attitude and directional indicators; below 4.5 inHg indicators not reliable
span 36 ft, length 26 ft 11 in (envelope only)

wing span 36 ft (note 1: shown with strobe lights installed); length 26 ft 11 in; height 8 ft 9½ in maximum (note 2: nose gear depressed, all tires and nose strut properly inflated, flashing beacon installed); horizontal tail span 11 ft 4 in; main wheel track 8 ft 4½ in; propeller arc 6 ft 3 in maximum; note 3: wheel base 65 in; note 4: propeller ground clearance 11¾ in; note 5: wing area 174 sq ft; note 6: minimum turning radius, pivot point to outboard wing tip, 27 ft 5½ in

firewall station 0; rear doorpost bulkhead station 65.3 (65¼ in aft of the firewall); 48¾ in from the instrument panel to that bulkhead; 42¾ in further to the aft cabin wall (station 108); aft baggage area 34 in long, to station 142
41 ahead of the front seats, 48 at the front seats, 43 at the rear seat, 33 in the baggage area, 10¼ in the aft baggage area

at the lower window line / at the cabin floor: 39½ / 34 at the front seats; 37½ / 29½ between the rear door posts; 38½ / 36 behind them; 35 / 25 and 33½ / 28 in the baggage area; 21½ at the aft end of the aft baggage area
cabin door: 32 wide at the top, 37 at the bottom, 40 high in front, 41 high at the rear; baggage door: 15¼ wide at top and bottom, 22 high in front, 21 high at the rear

single-slot type; electrically driven; switch lever on the instrument panel in a slotted panel with mechanical stops at 10° and 20°; scale and pointer beside the lever show flap travel in degrees; 15-ampere FLAP circuit breaker

tricycle; steerable nose wheel, two main wheels, wheel fairings; tubular spring-steel main gear struts; air/oil nose gear shock strut; hydraulically actuated disc brake on the inboard side of each main wheel, with a fairing over each brake
two areas: from the back of the rear seats to the aft cabin bulkhead, and one aft of that bulkhead; lockable baggage door on the left side; baggage net with tie-down straps

occupant centre of gravity: pilot and front passenger station 37 with the seat set for an average occupant (34 to 46); rear passengers station 73; baggage area 1 station 82 to 108 (arm 95); baggage area 2 station 108 to 142 (arm 123); datum station 0 is the front face of the firewall

two separate adjustable front seats (four-way or six-way), a split-backed fixed rear seat, optional child's seat; four-way: tubular handle under the centre of the seat for fore and aft, lever under the right front corner for the seat back angle; rear seat backs adjusted with a lever under each corner of the seat bottom

seat belts at all seats, attached to fittings on the floorboard, buckle half inboard and link half outboard of each front seat; front shoulder harness attached to the rear doorpost above the window line and stowed behind a sheath above the cabin door; integrated harness with inertia reels optional

two entry doors with a recessed exterior handle, an interior handle (OPEN, CLOSE, LOCK), a key-operated lock on the left door only and a door stop mechanism; openable window in the left door (right optional), held closed by a detent equipped latch on the lower edge of the window frame, with a spring-loaded retaining arm; may be opened up to 160 knots
shaped steel rod with a red metal flag, through the hole in the top of the pilot's control wheel shaft and the hole in the shaft collar on the instrument panel; the flag covers the ignition switch
separate adjustable ventilators: one near each upper corner of the windshield, two available for the rear cabin area

audio control panel with transmitter selector switch, automatic audio selector switch and audio selector switches (speaker or phone); microphone-headset with a keying switch on the left side of the pilot's control wheel, jacks near the lower left corner of the instrument panel; static dischargers recommended for IFR

instrument panel figure names, among others: light rheostat control knobs, lighter, map compartment, microphone, auxiliary mike jack, phone jack, rear view mirror, omni course indicators, ADF bearing indicator

preflight inspection: control wheel lock REMOVE; rudder gust lock REMOVE; tail, wing and nose tie-downs DISCONNECT; pitot tube cover REMOVE; sampler cup at each fuel tank sump quick-drain valve; strainer drain knob pulled for about four seconds; oil not less than four quarts
the airplane is most easily moved by hand with a tow bar attached to the nose gear strut; towed by a vehicle, the nose wheel must never be turned more than 30 degrees either side of centre

normal category: maximum takeoff weight 2300 lb and maximum landing weight 2300 lb; utility category: maximum takeoff weight 2000 lb and maximum landing weight 2000 lb, with the baggage compartment and the rear seat not occupied
baggage area 1 (or a passenger on the child's seat), station 82 to 108: 120 lb; baggage area 2, station 108 to 142: 50 lb; the maximum combined weight of the two areas is 120 lb

normal category: forward limit 35.0 in aft of the datum at 1950 lb or less, varying in a straight line to 38.5 in at 2300 lb; aft limit 47.3 in at all weights; utility category: forward limit 35.0 in at 1950 lb or less, varying in a straight line to 35.5 in at 2000 lb; aft limit 40.5 in at all weights; the reference datum is the lower portion of the front face of the firewall
normal category at 2300 lb: flaps up +3.8 g and -1.52 g, flaps down +3.0 g; utility category at 2000 lb: flaps up +4.4 g and -1.76 g, flaps down +3.0 g; the design load factors are 150% of these

normal category: non-aerobatic; approved are stalls except whip stalls, lazy eights, chandelles, and turns in which the bank is not more than 60 degrees; aerobatics including spins are not approved; utility category recommended entry speeds: chandelles 105 knots, lazy eights 105 knots, steep turns 95 knots, spins and stalls slow deceleration; abrupt use of the controls is prohibited above 97 knots; intentional spins with flaps extended are prohibited; the altitude lost in a stall recovery is 180 feet
the airplane is equipped for day VFR and may be equipped for night VFR and IFR; flight into known icing conditions is prohibited

two standard tanks of 21.5 gal each: total 43 gal, usable 40 gal, unusable 3 gal; two long-range tanks of 27 gal each: total 54 gal, usable 50 gal, unusable 4 gal; to ensure maximum fuel capacity when refuelling, put the fuel selector on LEFT or RIGHT to prevent cross-feeding; take off and land with the fuel selector on BOTH; approved grades are 100LL (blue) and 100 (green)

engine failure after takeoff: flaps up 65 KIAS, flaps down 60 KIAS; manoeuvring speed 97 KIAS at 2300 lb, 89 KIAS at 1950 lb, 80 KIAS at 1600 lb; maximum glide at 2300 lb 65 KIAS; precautionary landing with engine power 60 KIAS; landing without engine power: flaps up 65 KIAS, flaps down 60 KIAS
throttle IDLE, brakes APPLY, wing flaps RETRACT, mixture IDLE CUT-OFF, ignition switch OFF, master switch OFF
airspeed 65 KIAS flaps up, 60 KIAS flaps down; mixture IDLE CUT-OFF; fuel selector valve OFF; ignition switch OFF; wing flaps AS REQUIRED; master switch OFF

airspeed 65 KIAS flaps up, 60 KIAS flaps down; mixture IDLE CUT-OFF; fuel selector valve OFF; ignition switch OFF; wing flaps AS REQUIRED (40 degrees recommended); master switch OFF; doors UNLATCH prior to touchdown; touchdown SLIGHTLY TAIL LOW; brakes APPLY HEAVILY

wing flaps 20 degrees; airspeed 60 KIAS; selected field FLY OVER, noting terrain and obstructions, then retract flaps upon reaching a safe altitude and airspeed; avionics power switch and electrical switches OFF; wing flaps 40 degrees on final approach; airspeed 60 KIAS; master switch OFF; doors UNLATCH prior to touchdown; touchdown SLIGHTLY TAIL LOW; ignition switch OFF; brakes APPLY HEAVILY

continue cranking to get a start, which would suck the flames and accumulated fuel through the carburettor and into the engine; if the engine starts: power 1700 RPM for a few minutes, then shut down and inspect for damage; if it fails to start: throttle FULL OPEN, mixture IDLE CUT-OFF, continue cranking, fire extinguisher OBTAIN, engine SECURE (master switch OFF, ignition switch OFF, fuel selector valve OFF), extinguish the fire, inspect the fire damage before another flight

mixture IDLE CUT-OFF; fuel selector valve OFF; master switch OFF; cabin heat and air OFF except the overhead vents; airspeed 100 KIAS (if the fire is not extinguished, increase the glide speed to find an airspeed that will provide an incombustible mixture); forced landing EXECUTE as in the emergency landing without engine power

master switch OFF; avionics power switch OFF; all other switches except the ignition switch OFF; vents, cabin air and heat CLOSED; fire extinguisher ACTIVATE if available; if the fire appears out and electrical power is necessary for continuance of flight: master switch ON, circuit breakers CHECK for the faulty circuit and do not reset, radio switches OFF, avionics power switch ON, radio and electrical switches ON one at a time with a delay after each until the short circuit is localized; vents, cabin air and heat OPEN when the fire is completely extinguished

master switch OFF; vents, cabin air and heat CLOSED to avoid drafts; fire extinguisher ACTIVATE if available; after discharging an extinguisher in a closed cabin, ventilate the cabin; land as soon as possible to inspect for damage

retard the throttle to IDLE; ailerons NEUTRAL; apply and HOLD full rudder opposite to the direction of rotation; just AFTER the rudder reaches the stop, move the control wheel BRISKLY forward far enough to break the stall (full down elevator may be needed at aft centre of gravity loadings); HOLD these inputs until rotation stops; as rotation stops, neutralize the rudder and make a smooth recovery from the resulting dive

preflight inspection COMPLETE; seats, belts and shoulder harnesses ADJUST and LOCK; fuel selector valve BOTH; avionics power switch, autopilot and electrical equipment OFF (the avionics power switch must be OFF during engine start to prevent damage to avionics); brakes TEST and SET; circuit breakers CHECK IN

parking brake SET; cabin doors and windows CLOSED and LOCKED; flight controls FREE and CORRECT; flight instruments SET; fuel selector valve BOTH; mixture RICH (below 3000 feet); elevator trim and rudder trim TAKEOFF; throttle 1700 RPM; magnetos CHECK (RPM drop should not exceed 125 RPM on either magneto or 50 RPM differential between magnetos); carburettor heat CHECK for RPM drop; engine instruments and ammeter CHECK; suction gage CHECK; avionics power switch ON; radios SET; autopilot OFF; air conditioner OFF; flashing beacon, navigation lights and strobe lights ON as required; throttle friction lock ADJUST; brakes RELEASE
wing flaps UP; carburettor heat COLD; throttle FULL OPEN; elevator control LIFT NOSE WHEEL at 55 KIAS; climb speed 70 to 80 KIAS

wing flaps UP; carburettor heat COLD; brakes APPLY; throttle FULL OPEN; mixture RICH (above 3000 feet, LEAN to obtain maximum RPM); brakes RELEASE; elevator control SLIGHTLY TAIL LOW; climb speed 59 KIAS until all obstacles are cleared
power 2200 to 2700 RPM (no more than 75% is recommended); elevator trim and rudder trim ADJUST; mixture LEAN
seats, belts and harnesses SECURE; fuel selector valve BOTH; mixture RICH; carburettor heat ON (apply full heat before closing the throttle); autopilot OFF; air conditioner OFF
airspeed 60 to 70 KIAS flaps up; wing flaps AS DESIRED below 85 KIAS; airspeed 55 to 65 KIAS flaps down; touchdown MAIN WHEELS FIRST; landing roll LOWER NOSE WHEEL GENTLY; braking MINIMUM REQUIRED

airspeed 60 to 70 KIAS flaps up; wing flaps FULL DOWN (40 degrees); airspeed 60 KIAS until flare; power REDUCE to idle after clearing the obstacle; touchdown MAIN WHEELS FIRST; brakes APPLY HEAVILY; wing flaps RETRACT

throttle FULL OPEN; carburettor heat COLD; wing flaps 20 degrees immediately; climb speed 55 KIAS; wing flaps 10 degrees until obstacles are cleared, then RETRACT after reaching a safe altitude and 60 KIAS

after landing: wing flaps UP, carburettor heat COLD; securing the airplane: parking brake SET, avionics power switch, electrical equipment and autopilot OFF, mixture IDLE CUT-OFF (pulled full out), ignition switch OFF, master switch OFF, control lock INSTALL

figure 5-6 (time, fuel and distance to climb): add 1.1 gallons of fuel for engine start, taxi and takeoff allowance; the range and endurance profiles allow for this fuel and for the fuel used and distance covered in the climb, and keep a reserve of 45 minutes at 45% BHP, which is 4.1 gallons

airplane weighing form (figure 6-1): oil, no oil filter 6 qts at 7.5 lbs per gallon, arm -14.0; oil with oil filter 7 qts at 7.5 lbs per gallon, arm -14.0; unusable fuel, standard tanks 3 gal at 6 lbs per gallon, arm 46.0; long-range tanks 4 gal at 6 lbs per gallon, arm 46.0; the loading problem takes usable fuel at 6 lbs per gallon

sample loading problem (figure 6-5), in pounds and pound-inches divided by 1000: basic empty weight 1454 lb, 57.6; usable fuel, standard tanks 40 gal, 240 lb, 11.5; pilot and front passenger 340 lb, 12.6; rear passengers 170 lb, 12.4; baggage area 1 96 lb, 9.1; total 2300 lb, 103.2; the point (2300 lb at 103.2) falls within the centre of gravity moment envelope, so the loading is acceptable
